conviction_note: The findings split both ways. A full quarter of Tupperware, plus a peso about 8% stronger year on year, implies USD revenue a few percent above the thin aggregator consensus. Against that, the original standalone 4-8% guide looks unreachable after +2.2% organic growth in 1H, margins fell across all three brands in Q2, and the stock fell after each of its last three prints, including Q2, which beat. p_up is 45 on an abs move of 4.0, so the scaled number is -0.4, against an impact_sum of -1.0. Both are small because no single document-level fact decides the print.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue $262.8M and EPS $0.72 (Earnings Whispers, https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/bwmx, read 2026-10-22). A Benzinga snippet carries $261.4M and $0.71 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/BWMX/earnings-forecasts, snippet_only, page 403). A later EW snapshot in search read $267.85M. Two estimate sources roughly agree, but the coverage is 1-3 analysts and in USD on an MXN reporter, so the bar is soft. The company guide is FY2026 net revenue +18-22% on 2025's MXN 14,265m with an EBITDA margin of at least 19% (post-acquisition), beside the original +4-8% (Q2 2026 6-K Ex 99.1, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1788257/000121390026080912/ea029841201ex99-1.htm).
positioning_check: No options market: the baseline reads no_paired_strikes, so there is no skew and no implied move. Short interest at the 2026-06-30 FINRA settlement was about 130-138K shares, roughly 0.35% of float, with 1.7-3.0 days to cover and a 0.4% borrow fee (https://equibles.com/stocks/bwmx/summary, https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/bwmx/, both search snippets). I could not reach a later settlement. The short is not crowded. 20-day turnover is about 36.7K shares a day, roughly $0.58M, so the name is thin. Run-up is -4.19% over 20 days and -3.37% over 5, in step with the peso falling from about 16.9 to 18.4-18.7 per USD since late August. Earnings Whispers shows a post-earnings drift of -8.3% since the 2026-07-23 print.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 is the first full quarter of Tupperware LatAm, which BeFra did not own in Q3 2025, so the arithmetic points to USD revenue above consensus. Tupperware ran MXN 451m in June 2026 alone, about MXN 5,073m in 2025 (pro forma 19,338 less reported 14,265), or ~1,270 a quarter. Standalone BeFra did MXN 3,377m in Q3 2025 and grew +3.6% (Betterware) and +4.5% (Jafra) in Q2 2026. That gives MXN ~4,650-4,900m for Q3 2026. At the Q3 2026 average USD/MXN of about 17.1 (18.6 in Q3 2025) that is $272-287M, against a consensus of $262.8M (EW) or $261.4M (Benzinga): +3% to +9%. In MXN, the consensus is ~4,490m at 17.1.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-23 amc): revenue $239.3M against $229.1M consensus and EPS $0.57 against $0.52 per Benzinga, both beats, and the stock went 17.31 to 16.73 (-3.4%), then drifted -8.3% per EW. Q4 2025 (2026-02-26): -8.8%. Q1 2026 (2026-04-23): -2.1%. Q3 2025 (2025-10-23): +2.9%. Q2 2025: +13.0%. From Yahoo daily closes (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/BWMX?range=2y&interval=1d). The name has sold its last three prints, beats included.
findings.why_not_priced: The consensus is 1-3 analysts, carried in USD for a company that reports in MXN, and the converted MXN figure (~4,490m) sits below simple run-rate arithmetic. If the market had priced a beat, the stock would not be at -4.2% over 20 days and 19% off its high going into the print. But the market may simply expect what the guide implies (see the guidance findings), so the gap could be an FX or definition artefact.
findings.independence: FX from Yahoo MXN=X (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/MXN=X?range=9mo&interval=1wk). The Q3 2025 base is from the FY2025 6-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1788257/000121390026020857/ea0278472-ex991.htm). This shares the Q2 release with the guidance findings below.

findings.finding: The original standalone FY2026 guide of +4.0-8.0% net revenue now looks out of reach. Standalone 1H 2026 revenue was MXN ~7,220m (reported 7,671 less June Tupperware 451) against 7,062m in 1H 2025, i.e. +2.2%. Hitting the guide would need roughly +6-14% in 2H against a September ANTAD backdrop of +0.9%. The company said it would show both the original and the updated guide through year-end, so Q3 is the point where the original is visibly missed or cut. FY2025 went the same way: revised to 1-5%, met at the low end, EBITDA below guidance.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025 (2026-02-26) carried the FY2025 low-end revenue result and an EBITDA miss against guidance, and the stock fell 18.17 to 16.57 (-8.8%) (Yahoo chart, above). Q2 2026 printed 1H organic growth below guide and fell -3.4%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The 1H organic number has been public since July, and the stock's -8.3% post-Q2 drift probably reflects some of it. What is not public is whether management formally lowers the 4-8%, or keeps the consolidated 18-22% and lets the original fade. A formal cut on the call would be a new event.
findings.independence: The FY2025 history is from the FY2025 6-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1788257/000121390026020857/ea0278472-ex991.htm). The macro backdrop is ANTAD September 2026 (https://elceo.com/negocios/el-palacio-de-hierro-coppel-suburbia-registran-peor-desempeno-antad/). Same guidance table as the next finding.

findings.finding: The post-acquisition FY2026 guide of +18-22% (MXN ~16,830-17,400m) looks conservative on simple arithmetic. Seven months of Tupperware at its 2025 run-rate (~MXN 423m a month; June was 451) is ~2,960m, or +20.8% of 2025's 14,265m on its own. Add even the +2.2% standalone growth of 1H and the arithmetic gives ~+23%, so with a full Tupperware quarter in hand the consolidated range could be raised or narrowed upward on the Q3 release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide was raised to 18-22% with the Q2 release on 2026-07-23 (a mechanical acquisition add), and the stock fell -3.4%. No precedent for an organic-driven raise in the window I checked.
findings.why_not_priced: Inference from the company's own pro forma figures that no aggregator surfaces. If the market priced a raise, the stock would not have drifted -8% since July. The counter is that management may have deliberately embedded a weaker 2H for Tupperware (Brazil revenue still declining, under -7% in June) or for standalone organic, so the guide could be held.
findings.independence: Same Q2 release as the original-guide finding. The two are compatible: the consolidated guide can be held or raised by Tupperware while the standalone guide is cut. The pro forma 1H 2026 figure of MXN 9,490m is in the same release.

findings.finding: The margin comparison is hard. Standalone Q3 2025 EBITDA was MXN 722.1m at a 21.4% margin, the highest of FY2025. In Q2 2026 EBITDA margin fell year on year in every brand: Betterware 19.5% (-42bp), Jafra 16.5% (-199bp), Tupperware 27.4% (-418bp against June 2025 pro forma). Betterware also flagged temporary logistics costs tied to the Strait of Hormuz. So organic EBITDA is likely down year on year in Q3 even as consolidated EBITDA rises on Tupperware. The partial offset is a peso about 8% stronger year on year in Q3, which lowers the landed cost of China-sourced Betterware goods, while Mexico's 5-50% tariffs on non-FTA imports, in force since 2026-01-01, push the other way.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: organic EBITDA and net income down (Jafra gross-margin investment, Tupperware deal costs) despite a headline beat, and the stock fell -3.4%. Q4 2025: margin below the prior year and EBITDA below guidance, -8.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: The EPS consensus of $0.72 is one number in USD and does not show whether analysts model organic margin compression against a 21.4% comp. The headline consolidated EBITDA will rise sharply year on year, so the compression only shows in the brand tables, which wire headlines do not carry.
findings.independence: Q2 brand margins are in the Q2 6-K Ex 99.1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1788257/000121390026080912/ea029841201ex99-1.htm). The tariff context is from El Imparcial (https://www.elimparcial.com/dinero/2025/12/30/a-partir-del-1-de-enero-del-2026-mexico-aplicara-aranceles-a-china-de-hasta-el-50/), and the company has not quantified the tariff effect.

findings.finding: The peso has fallen from about 16.9 per USD (late August) to 18.4-18.7 (October): the September depreciation wiped out its gains for the year, and the Banxico FIX was 18.49 on 2026-10-16. That is a forward headwind to Betterware's USD-denominated import costs for Q4 and 2027 and to USD translation of Q4 results, so the Q4 margin commentary on the call could be cautious.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean precedent found. The ADS fell -4.2% over 20 days alongside a ~7-9% peso move, so the translation is largely already in the price.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced through the ADS translation. What is not priced is the company's own statement of hedge cover and Q4 gross margin, which nobody has outside the company. Hence the small size.
findings.independence: Yahoo MXN=X weekly closes (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/MXN=X?range=9mo&interval=1wk). This is a proxy: the company has not commented on its 2H FX hedging.

findings.finding: Mexican discretionary retail was weak late in Q3: ANTAD September 2026 same-store sales +0.9%, total +3.7%, department stores -0.8% same-store. That fits low single-digit standalone growth for Betterware and Jafra, the direct-selling businesses that make up ~94% of 1H revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 release cited soft consumption and FX effects in northern Mexico, and the stock fell -3.4%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a public macro series, so it is likely partly priced. Its transmission to a direct-selling catalogue business is unconfirmed. Filed small, as a proxy.
findings.independence: Proxy only. It points the same way as the original-guide finding (low organic growth) but is a separate series. No company or counterparty confirmation.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-29 the company called an Ordinary Shareholders' Meeting for 2026-10-16 with a single substantive item: approval of a dividend. The amount is not in the notice and will most likely be announced with the release, as the MXN 250m Q2 dividend was on 2026-07-23. The prior pattern is MXN 200m, 200m, then 250m after the acquisition, the 26th consecutive quarterly payment, while reported net debt/EBITDA is 2.57x (1.62x pro forma).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The dividend was raised from 200m to 250m alongside the Q2 print, and the stock still fell -3.4%. Dividend news has not visibly moved this name.
findings.why_not_priced: The amount is unknown. A cut would signal deleveraging pressure and a hold or raise would confirm the policy. The continuity is largely expected.
findings.independence: The Business Wire Q2 dividend release shows the pattern (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260723382551/en/).

baseline_tension: There are no skew or options to cut against. The -4.2% 20-day run-up tracks the peso, and the name's record of selling its last three prints (beats included) argues against reading the arithmetic revenue beat as an upside move. That is why p_up sits below 50 despite a likely positive print_vs_bar.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the Tupperware-driven revenue beat went from +1.0 to +0.6 because the Q2 2026 beat was sold (-3.4%, -8.3% drift); p_up from 46 to 45.

Rule 6 (verify the bar): the bar rests on two roughly agreeing aggregator sources ($262.8M EW, $261.4M Benzinga snippet) for a 1-3 analyst USD consensus on an MXN reporter. Treated as soft, with no finding sized above 1.0.

Rule 5 (proxies) and the base-rate rule: the ANTAD and peso findings stay small and are labelled as proxies; the reaction base rate was rebuilt from confirmed release dates rather than the baseline's 6-K matches.
Rule 3 (read the set): the two guidance findings were checked for contradiction and are compatible (standalone cut, consolidated held or raised), so both were kept with the shared document noted.
